questions.question:

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

Men __never have managed__ to abolish wars up to now but maybe they will find a way in future.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**have never managed**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence uses "**never have managed**," which is the present perfect form.
 
• This construction emphasizes that from the past up to the present moment, men have not succeeded in abolishing wars.
 
• The alternative "**never managed**" would suggest a **simple past** tense, which would alter the meaning by not emphasizing the ongoing nature of the action.
 
• "**Have never managed**" maintains the correct tense and emphasizes the ongoing nature of the action.
 
• The concept at play here is the use of the **present perfect tense** to convey an action that started in the past and continues into the present.
 
• In this case, the action is the attempt to abolish wars. 
 
• 
 
So, the correct choice, "have never managed," aligns with the intended meaning, emphasizing the continuous effort from the past until the present regarding the abolition of wars.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence**: *Men have never managed to abolish wars up to now but maybe they will find a way in future. *
